---
title: "Faceting"
description: "Small multiples: one panel per level of a grouping variable with facet_wrap()."
categories: [Composition]
---



`facet_wrap()` splits the data into a panel per group, sharing scales so the
panels are directly comparable.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p <- vplot(mtcars, width = 8, height = 3.4) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>
  facet_wrap(~cyl) |>
  labs(title = "Weight vs. mpg, faceted by cylinder count")
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/facets.png){width=100%}
:::
:::


## Strip labels

The `labeller` argument controls the strip text. `label_both` names the
variable alongside its value, which a grid of bare numbers badly needs.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p_grid <- vplot(mtcars, width = 8, height = 4.4) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>
  facet_grid(am ~ cyl, labeller = label_both) |>
  labs(title = "facet_grid() with label_both")
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/facets-label-both.png){width=100%}
:::
:::


Long values can wrap onto several lines with `label_wrap_gen(width)`, and the
strips grow to fit. A named character vector works as a lookup table.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cars <- transform(
  mtcars,
  trans = ifelse(am == 1, "manual gearbox, driver shifts", "automatic gearbox")
)

p_wrap <- vplot(cars, width = 8, height = 3.4) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>
  facet_wrap(~trans, labeller = label_wrap_gen(18)) |>
  labs(title = "label_wrap_gen(18)")
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/facets-label-wrap.png){width=100%}
:::
:::


## A legend per panel

Colour is shared across panels by default, so one legend covers the figure.
When each panel holds its own set of categories, `resolve_scale(color =
"independent")` trains the colour scale per panel, spending the whole palette
on that panel's levels, and gives each panel its own legend, titled with its
strip.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p_indep <- vplot(mtcars, width = 8, height = 3.4) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(gear)) |>
  facet_wrap(~cyl, ncol = 3, labeller = label_both) |>
  resolve_scale(color = "independent") |>
  labs(color = "gears", title = "An independent colour scale in each panel")
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/facets-independent.png){width=100%}
:::
:::
